messages:
maria: Quick check — trying to onboard a customer that spans two orgs. We impersonate a svcacct in infra-project-A, exchange for an OIDC token with target_audience set to their sink, but the streaming client fails with:

samir: Error?

maria: It rejects because aud claims contains `https://api.redwood.com/org/ORG_ID` instead of the expected `urn:redwood:project:PROJECT_ID` the client validates. Happens in both Python and Go SDK.

jamal: Hmm, are you doing an Identity Token (id_token) exchange or a JWT assertion? The audience semantics differ. If you call the OAuth token endpoint with `audience` you get an OIDC token whose `aud` is literally that string. If you're using STS or impersonation we sometimes produce org-scoped aud.

elaine: For context — our streaming client lib (go/streaming) enforces aud match to the pinned project id for security. We landed that check to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

maria: Right — customer wants single token that can target multiple downstream projects in their org. Can we relax the client or recommend a flow?

samir: Two options: 1) Issue a token whose audience is the specific downstream resource (recommended). 2) Keep current token and have the client accept a set of allowed audiences (configurable). Option 2 requires an explicit allowlist and audit.

ricardo: For async onboarding quick hack, we often mint a service account token in the exact target project (impersonate:system:projects/-/serviceAccounts/target-sa@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com). That produces the right aud. Caveat: requires cross-project iam/roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator permissions.

maria: Sharing sample exchange we tried (python):
```python
# using oauth token exchange to get id_token
resp = requests.post('https://sts.example/token', data={
  'grant_type': 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange',
  'subject_token': svcacct_jwt,
  'subject_token_type': 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt',
  'audience': 'urn:redwood:project:TARGET-PROJ'
})
````

jamal: That should yield aud=urn:redwood:project:TARGET-PROJ. If you still see org-scoped aud, the impersonation layer might be rewriting audience, or you might be hitting the generic org-identity endpoint.

devx-bot: FYI docs: https://intra.redwood.dev/auth/impersonation#token-exchange (internal) :link:

elaine: Also flagged an SDK nuance: Go client uses jwt package that demands `aud` is a string or array; Python accepts array too. If we relax client check to allow array containment it may be backward compatible.

samir: Agree — change would be small: treat aud as array, accept if any member matches allowed project aud. Need security signoff.

maria: Can someone drop a small PR to relax the Go aud check and add a config toggle? I'll run it against the customer's sandbox this week.

jamal: I can pick the PR. Ping me on the review, I'll add unit tests and a short note in changelog.

maria: Thanks! tagging @jamal for review when ready. Also logging action: update onboarding doc with recommended impersonation permissions and the sample exchange above.

ricardo: Re: retries — if token exchange fails transiently our streaming reconnect loop should backoff but keep attempting exchange. We had a bug where token refresh was throttling and caused immediate stream close. If you hit that, ping eng-runtime.

maria: Noted. I'll capture logs and post if it recurs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
